directive.quote: Please own ONLY src/record_write_model.rs and src/store.rs metadata coverage
directive.source: Authorized coordinator assignment within source:Y29kZXgtZ2VuZXJpYy1pbnRha2UtbGlmZWN5Y2xlLTIwMjYtMTEtMDc; not a new person message.

preserve: src/record_write_model.rs: live declarations remain DATA; unknown properties remain open, shipped properties take precedence, and unchanged legacy values do not fail a changed-field check. Ordered effective batch declarations exclude no-op envelopes.

src/store.rs: the scoped SQLite adapter keeps current records and an append-only change/retry receipt atomically, checks admitted authority at its transaction boundaries, and refuses different input under an existing request key. Point, list and change readers preserve account/resource scope.
allowed_deltas: The cited JavaScript model has generic declaration and value-kind checks. Rust additionally interprets DATA-declared choices, person-present marks and allowed moves, including missing/null field release and kind-change release. The old slices do not implement those Rust move restrictions; no historical move-check parity is claimed.

The retired own-resource transaction and record read/write facade are behavioral predecessors for the scoped Store, not its schema or byte-copy baseline. Rust uses explicit account/resource/id keys, expected versions, tombstones, immutable retry rows and byte-bounded pages. It does not restore the old Worker, EEAF decomposed tables, product operations or cloud ownership.

The current Store read_existing/read_existing_current/has_record additions delegate to the existing SQLite/storage owner: read-only live-WAL access to an existing file, moved-source refusal and retained tombstone identity lookup. These native additions have no direct JavaScript file-open counterpart in the cited slices. They do not create a missing journal or claim an unseen execution.
banned_substitutions: Changing either Rust target or its existing DATA/model owner to obtain metadata coverage.
Claiming all historical model, history, EEAF or resource-command behavior is implemented by these two targets.
A source-first, byte-copy, new-test-pass, installed-engine or customer-delivery claim from this postimplementation declaration.
